$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages -- ui, js, php, py -- are generated from this directory and are never edited. Fix this file, then regenerate. This is the CONNECTOR half of Tynn #9 (MOIC's meeting bot) -- the stable Meet REST API v2, verified against its own Discovery Document (https://meet.googleapis.com/$discovery/rest?version=v2) on 2026-09-16. The BOT RUNTIME -- a service that actually joins a call and streams live media -- is explicitly the owner's call and not this estate's; Meet's own path there is the Media API, developer-preview and receive-only as of this writing, which is why a LIVE transcript and live participant status (waiting room/admitted/left) are not offered here. What the stable API gives instead: create a space (a join link), and read what happened after the fact -- conference records, participants, and the post-meeting transcript.
title: Google Meet

authorize.$comment: Every Meet API v2 call is a Bearer token on the Authorization header.

oauth.$refreshTokenRotates: Google's OAuth2 refresh tokens are reusable and do not rotate on refresh; the standard documented behaviour every other Google provider in this estate already declares the same way (google-calendar, google-sheets, …).
oauth.$grantComment: ONE consent grant shared by every Google connector (MOIC #1, 2026-11-08). A host may run them all on one OAuth client: request each feature's scopes when it is first used, with include_granted_scopes=true, and Google's new token covers every scope granted before. A refresh token comes back only on the FIRST code exchange with access_type=offline, so keep the stored one when an exchange returns none. Revoking ANY token removes the person's WHOLE grant -- every Google connector, not this one -- so a per-feature disconnect stops using the scope locally and only a full Google disconnect revokes. Identify the account by the id_token's sub (request openid; verify iss and aud = clientId), never by email.
oauth.$restrictedScopesComment: Google's RESTRICTED tier puts the whole OAuth client under verification and an annual CASA assessment. None of this connector's scopes is restricted.
oauth.$scopeComment: meetings.space.created is what space_create and space_get need ("conferences created by the app"). meetings.space.readonly is what conference_record_list, participant_list, transcript_list and transcript_entry_list need -- Google's own wording is broader ("any of your Google Meet conferences"), not only app-created ones. A host that only asks for one gets a 4xx on the other, not a silent gap.
oauth.$comment: Authorization Code. Google's discovery document declares no PKCE requirement for this API beyond what every Google OAuth2 client already follows; not declared here for the same reason it is not declared on google-calendar or google-sheets.

$sandboxComment: UNVERIFIED, not NONE. Google's own Meet API overview says nothing about a separate test estate, and nobody has confirmed there is truly nothing rather than simply not having found it -- checked 2026-09-16. Every call reaches a real Google account's real Meet spaces.
sandboxNote: Google Meet has no test estate distinct from a real account, as far as this review found (2026-09-16) -- but it is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed. space_create makes a real, joinable meeting space. Use fake mode while building.
summary: Create Google Meet spaces and read conference records, participants and transcripts.
$setupComment: Steps read from Google's docs on 2026-11-14 (each cites its page). Every Google connector shares one grant, so the first four steps are the same for all of them; do them once.

setup.title: Create (or reuse) the Google Cloud project for {{appName}}
setup.detail: Every Google connector shares ONE consent grant (oauth.grant "google"), so use one project and one OAuth client for all of them: one consent and one refresh token per person.

setup.title: Enable the Google Meet REST API
setup.detail: Console: APIs & Services, Library; open the Google Meet REST API and click Enable.

setup.title: Configure the consent screen
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Branding (app name {{appName}}, support email, contact email), then Audience: Internal for people inside your Google Workspace organisation only, or External (while it is in testing, add each tester under Test users). Then Data Access, Add or Remove Scopes, and add `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.created`, `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/meetings.space.readonly` beside the scopes of any other Google connector you use. You cannot remove the consent screen once it is configured.

setup.title: Create a Web application OAuth client
setup.detail: Console: Google Auth platform, Clients, Create Client; type Web application. Under Authorized redirect URIs click Add URI and paste {{oauthRedirectUrl}}, then Create. Copy the client ID and client secret when the client is created.

setup.title: Connect an account and check it works
setup.detail: Connect one Google account through {{appName}}'s OAuth flow, then run the check below.
setup.prompt: Using {{appName}}'s {{connector}} connection, run conference_record_list and report how many records it returns.
setup.done: conference_record_list answers for the connected account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client ID
credentialFields.help: From the Google Cloud project you registered. One value for the whole installation -- the same app serves every connected Google account.

credentialFields.label: OAuth client secret
credentialFields.help: From the same Google Cloud project. Used to exchange the code and to refresh; never sent with an API request.

credentialFields.label: Access token
credentialFields.help: Obtained by the host's OAuth exchange, PER CONNECTED GOOGLE ACCOUNT. Expires after one hour -- a host that does not refresh will work for a while and then fail with no warning.

credentialFields.label: Refresh token
credentialFields.help: Also per account. Reusable -- Google does not rotate it on refresh.
